issues.reason: The appositive NP "Democrat of West Virginia" is coreferential with Rockefeller, so there is no separate role referent for the of-phrase to attach to; *Complements of nouns and adjectives* keeps a true relational role noun's of-phrase on the ordinary genitive Possession (possessed first — the "sister of" / "capital of" precedent), which is exactly (Possession john_d_rockefeller_iv west_virginia), and the reviewer's own q2 gap concedes this is missing-witness coverage, not a falsehood.

The letter half stands — the seal-projection rule names only a definite's Member / Name typing atom, so PartOf is not explicitly licensed to sit outside — but the defect half does not: "provision of the Senate bill" presupposes the part-whole link independently of the sealed claim, so nothing false or over-asserted is at top level and no repair is warranted.

gaps_confirmed: An appositive NP carrying its own PP complement ("Democrat of West Virginia"): the appositive yields only a typing atom, so the complement has no witness to attach to.

A proper-noun modifier inside a common-noun compound ("the Senate bill"): *Compound concepts* excludes proper nouns, while *Names and casing* would read the capitalized run as the name and the adjacent lowercase noun as its kind, which is wrong here (the bill is not named "Senate").
new_gaps: Where a definite referent's non-typing description atoms (PartOf / Possession / a preposition-named oblique) go relative to a seal is unstated — the projection rule enumerates only Member / Name.
"that provision of the Senate bill" is structurally ambiguous between complementizer-plus-bare-NP and demonstrative NP with a zero complementizer; nothing selects a reading.
